entries.subject: DAMIT 2012: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-2012.txt. Model 2012, version 2018-07-18, pole (64°, -66°), period 11.06207 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: No registered reusable surface imagery was examined for the selected convex model. The grid marks missing imagery; the AKARI thermal size is a separate scale decision, not a surface map or terrain qualification.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Other DAMIT shape solutions
entries.finding: The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 2013: pole (252°, -14°), 11.06211 h, version 2018-07-18. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: Independent shape, spin or scale evidence distinguishes these alternatives, or a changed release offers a demonstrably better supported model.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA thermal scale
entries.finding: The retained AcuA row 2204 (Lyyli; three detections) supplies a 27.12 ± 1.31 km fitted nonrotating-sphere effective diameter. The recipe transfers it uniformly to the uncalibrated DAMIT 2012 mesh as an approximate volume scale. The catalog error is thermal-model/statistical only; it does not establish total size uncertainty, local shape accuracy, terrain or imagery. The retrieved original catalogue row was compared field-for-field with the retained row and matches.

entries.subject: Historical model and population records
entries.finding: Historical review retained the Ďurech et al. (2018) model-publication record and JPL SBDB Mars-crosser classification from the former README survey. They provide source context only: neither selects between the two DAMIT poles nor qualifies terrain, imagery or the AKARI scale.
